A snowball is melting in the sun and slowly shrinking. Determine the rate at which the surface area of the snowball is decreasing, given that the radius is decreasing at a rate of $\frac{1}{5}\,\text{in/s}$ and its surface area at that moment is $100\pi \,{\text{in}}^{2}.$ Do not round the answer.

*Hint*: Assume that the rate of decrease is positive.

The surface area of the snowball is decreasing at a rate of 
{{field-1}} ${\text{in}}^{2}/\text{s}.$
worked_solution:
Let $r$ be the radius of the snowball and let $A$ be its surface area. Both $r$ and $A$ change with time. In particular, we are given that

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}=-\frac{1}{5}\,\text{in/s},
$$

and we want to find $\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}$ when $A=100\pi \,{\text{in}}^{2}.$

To start, let's write down the formula for the surface area of a sphere and then differentiate it using implicit differentiation. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =4\pi {r}^{2} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(A) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\pi {r}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(A) & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}r}(4\pi {r}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}\cdot 8\pi r\end{aligned}
$$

We then calculate the value of $r$ using $A=100\pi .$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =4\pi {r}^{2} \\ 100\pi  & =4\pi {r}^{2} \\ 25 & ={r}^{2} \\ r & =\pm 5\end{aligned}
$$

Since radius cannot be negative, we have $r=5.$

We now substitute $\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}=-\frac{1}{5}$ and $r=5$ into our expression for $\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =-\frac{1}{5}\cdot 8\pi \cdot 5 \\ \frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =-8\pi \end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that the surface area of the snowball is decreasing at a rate of $8\pi \,{\text{in}}^{2}\text{/s}.$
